# The working life of Gwydion: from the myths to the modern trades

The myths did not retire. They moved offices. This is the file on where **Gwydion** works now.

Gwydion fab Dôn is the enchanter of the Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi, 'Math fab Mathonwy': nephew of Math the king of Gwynedd, brother of Gilfaethwy, and the foremost magician of medieval Welsh literature. He is poet, trickster, foster-father, and avenger in one figure — the man who makes illusions that pass for wealth, who pays for his crimes in animal skins, and who ends the tale as the careful hand that puts a broken world back into shape.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **3 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Gwydion
- **Pantheon:** Celtic
- **Domain of influence:** Magic, Poetry, Trickery
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Society & Spirit · Energy & Natural World · Commerce & Governance
- **Strongest seat:** Astrology, Tarot & Esoteric Services
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 158 of 449

## The Myth at Work

**The War for the Swine.** King Math of Gwynedd could live only with his feet in the lap of a virgin, except in time of war, and the maiden Goewin held that office.  When Gilfaethwy desired her, Gwydion devised the remedy: war. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

**The Punishment of the Brothers.** Math's justice is the strangest in the Mabinogi.  He struck Gwydion and Gilfaethwy with his magic wand and turned them into a stag and a hind, and sent them into the wild for a year; when they returned with a fawn, he made them a boar and a sow for the second year, and a wolf and a she-wolf for the third. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Astrology, Tarot & Esoteric Services

*Astrology apps, tarot, and spiritual guidance. (Sector: Society & Spirit)*

*The enchanter of the Fourth Branch — shape-shifting, flower-bride crafting, the eagle called down the oak.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest

*Farming, grain, food production, and agtech. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*The swine-trick — the magician who conjured pigs from reeds and destabilized two kingdoms with them.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Legal, Justice & Compliance

*Law, courts, and regulatory compliance. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

*The crafted justice of the ending — the owl-shape for Blodeuwedd, the spear through Llech Gronw; punishment engineered to fit the crime.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Gwydion performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

## The Long Employment

Gwydion's afterlife runs from Welsh tradition into modern letters.  Later Welsh usage named the Milky Way Caer Gwydion, 'Gwydion's fortress' — the enchanter's castle written across the night sky — and the antiquarian bards kept his tree-battle in the poetic canon. The age changed. The work did not.

If you work in astrology, tarot & esoteric services, agriculture, food & harvest, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/gwydion/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
